request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Hospital Course Summary:

This 47-year-old male patient was admitted to our institution with a diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with multiple mutations, including DNMT3A, RUNX1, and U2AF1, along with FLT3–ITD mutation. The patient had received various treatments for his condition but did not respond well to them. After a bone marrow analysis, emergent BCR–ABL1 rearrangement was detected along with increased allelic ratio of FLT3-ITD mutation. The patient was then treated with different therapies, including CPX-351 plus venetoclax, ponatinib, and gilteritinib combination, which resulted in a marrow remission. The patient underwent allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (ASCT) and achieved full remission on day 30 post-ASCT. Unfortunately, the patient expired 8 months after ASCT due to infectious complications.

Summary of Hospital Stay:
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment: CPX-351, decitabine, FLAG-IDA, single-agent gilteritinib, cladribine, idarubicin, cytarabine, sorafenib, decitabine, venetoclax, ponatinib, CPX-351 plus venetoclax, ponatinib, and gilteritinib combination, Allogeneic stem-cell transplantation
Complications: infectious complications
Outcome: Achieved Marrow remission; Achieved full remission post-ASCT

Assessment and Plan:

The patient presented with AML with FLT3–ITD, DNMT3A, RUNX1, and U2AF1 mutations that were resistant to several chemotherapy treatments. After various therapies, the patient achieved a marrow remission with the CPX-351 plus venetoclax, ponatinib, and gilteritinib combination. Allogeneic stem-cell transplantation was performed, which resulted in full remission post-ASCT. Despite successful remission, the patient died eight months post-ASCT due to infectious complications.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis is acute myeloid leukaemia, which falls under C92 (myeloid leukaemia). The codes in this block are C92.0 for acute myeloid leukaemia, not having achieved remission, and C92.00 for AML without remission in ICD-10-AM. The three-character category is C92 either way.

The case also involves a BCR-ABL1 rearrangement, which could raise the question of mixed-phenotype or Ph-positive leukaemia. Since the case is described as AML with an emergent BCR-ABL1 rearrangement, C92 remains the best fit.

CODE: C92
